```{r tbl-rf-attribution}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Provenance of the methodological claims in the Random Forest section"
#| tbl-pos: H

rf_attr <- tribble(
  ~Q, ~ML, ~Rel, ~Own,

  "Can it handle sparse, high-dimensional portfolios?",
  "Feature subsampling at each split avoids the small-n, large-p problem (Breiman 2001)",
  "Used on sparse export and patent baskets (Tacchella et al. 2023; Albora et al. 2023)",
  "That NUTS2 portfolios are sparse in exactly this way",

  "Can it capture what linear aggregation cannot?",
  "Importance decomposes across all interaction terms (Louppe et al. 2013)",
  "Summing pairwise relatedness is an oversimplification (Tacchella et al. 2023)",
  "Reading these interactions as capability complementarities",

  "Can it stay interpretable?",
  "Importance aggregates each predictor's contribution across trees (Breiman 2001)",
  "Importances can form a technology network (Fessina et al. 2024)",
  "Deriving both constructs from one estimation",

  "Is it stable at our sample size?",
  "Bagging reduces the variance of single trees (Breiman 1996)",
  "—",
  "Moderate n per technology-year model",

  "What can it not do?",
  "Gini importance is biased; correlated features mask one another (Strobl et al. 2007; Louppe et al. 2013)",
  "—",
  "A weak FITS edge may reflect masking, not absence of dependence"
)

rf_attr |>
  gt(groupname_col = "Q") |>
  cols_label(
    ML   = "Machine learning literature",
    Rel  = "Relatedness literature",
    Own  = "Our own claim"
  ) |>
  cols_width(
    ML   ~ pct(40),
    Rel  ~ pct(32),
    Own  ~ pct(28)
  ) |>
  tab_style(
    style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
    locations = cells_row_groups()
  ) |>
  tab_options(
    table.width               = pct(100),
    table.font.size           = px(12),
    data_row.padding          = px(4),
    column_labels.font.weight = "bold"
  )
```

## The distance variable {#sec-app-distance}

FITS weights are predictive associations: a higher weight means a closer relationship.
We therefore use the inverse of a weight as the length of the corresponding edge, $\ell_{s \to t} = 1/W_{s \to t}$, with weights below 0.001 set to 0.001 to avoid division by zero.
Because the network is directed, the shortest path from $s$ to $t$ generally differs from the path from $t$ to $s$.
We compute the weighted shortest path in both directions, and keep the shorter of the two as the distance between the two technologies:

$$d(s,t) = \min\left\{\text{sp}(s \to t),\; \text{sp}(t \to s)\right\}$$ {#eq-app-distance-pair}

The distance of technology $t$ for region $r$ is the distance from the closest technology in the region's portfolio:

$$\text{rawdist}_{r,t,y} = \min_{s:\,\text{RTA}_{r,s,y} \geq 1} d(s,t)$$ {#eq-app-distance}

Keeping the shorter direction loses the information on which technology predicts which.
We accept this to keep the later models tractable.
When no path connects a technology to the regional portfolio, the distance is missing.

## Entry benchmark: the part of potential that density does not explain {#sec-app-benchmark}

This section reports two checks on the entry benchmark (Model 0).
@tbl-bench-diag shows how strongly potential and relatedness density are correlated, and whether their joint estimation is affected by collinearity.
@tbl-bench-models repeats the benchmark with the standardised residual from regressing potential on relatedness density ("Resid"), which is the part of potential that density does not explain.

```{r}
#| echo: false
bench <- readRDS(here::here("resources/benchmark_check.rds"))
```

```{r tbl-bench-diag}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Collinearity diagnostics, Model 0"
#| tbl-pos: H
bench$diagnostics |>
  gt::gt() |>
  gt::fmt_number(Value, decimals = 3)
```

```{r tbl-bench-models}
#| echo: false
#| tbl-cap: "Entry benchmark with the orthogonal component of Potential"
#| tbl-pos: H
modelsummary::modelsummary(
  bench$models,
  stars = c("*" = .05, "**" = .01, "***" = .001),
  coef_map = c(
    "relatedness_density" = "Relatedness density",
    "pred11"              = "Potential",
    "resid_z"             = "Resid",
    "patent_n"            = "Patent count",
    "reg_comp"            = "Regional complexity",
    "tech_comp"           = "Technology complexity"
  ),
  gof_map = c("nobs", "r2.within", "rmse"),
  notes = "All models include region and year fixed effects; standard errors clustered by region and technology. 'Resid' is the standardised residual from regressing Potential on relatedness density."
)
```
